# kurasu: web rules

verified: 2026-11-02

Answers how kurasu's web is built: how screens share pieces, how they reach the API and where files go.

## Knowledge

- A piece used by both the student and the teacher is one component. The common part is inside it, and what each side adds enters through slots: a `ReactNode` prop for a fixed place, or a function that receives the row (`renderActions`, `renderHand`) for a per-row place. There is no admin flag.
- In program designs, slots follow the notation of the plugin's `component-tree` reference: `<slot>`.
- API access follows the wiki entry `tanstack-query/operation-hooks`: one hook per operation in `apps/web/src/features/<topic>/<hook>.ts`, keys from `queryKeys`, and typed `options` passed through. Each operation hook is built on `useApiQuery` or `useApiMutation` (`apps/web/src/api/`), which call `runApi` with the Effect HttpApi client. A screen never calls `useQuery` or `useMutation` directly. A query whose `queryOptions` are shared with a non-hook caller calls `useQuery` over those options instead: `useMaterialFile` (shared with the slides check).
- An operation hook does not list its errors by hand. Its `options` take `EndpointError<"group", "endpoint">` (`apps/web/src/api/api-error.ts`), which reads the error type of that endpoint from the HttpApi client: the endpoint's own errors, its middleware's (`Unauthenticated`, `NoAccess`, `NotTeacher`), `HttpClientError` and `SchemaError`. `useApiQuery` and `useApiMutation` infer the error type from `call` too, so options that name another endpoint's errors fail to typecheck. An endpoint without the login middleware, such as `auth.requestLink`, has no `Unauthenticated` in its errors.
- `useApiMutation` runs the hook's own callbacks before the screen's, and invalidates its `invalidates` keys before the screen's `onSuccess`, so the screen always sees fresh data.
- An instant action passes `optimistic` to `useApiMutation`: a list of entries built with `optimisticPatch({ key, exact?, patch })` (`api/optimistic-patch.ts`). `key` is a function of the input, because some keys name one record, such as one session. `exact` is for a key that is a prefix of other keys holding another data type. The mutation cancels and snapshots those keys, patches them before the request, puts the snapshot back on failure and invalidates after a failure too. Moving the slide is the exception: `useMoveSlide` has no patch, and `useSlideMoves` keeps the shown position in the screen while moves save one at a time, keeping only the last, because late answers would send a patched cache back.
- A mutation's `errorToast` is a function of the input that returns the toast text, or `undefined` for no toast. `useVote` takes `inlineError` from its caller instead of reading the input: the word cloud and the feedback show their error inline, choice and scale votes show a toast. An access error shows no toast; the query client sends the user to the login instead.
- The toast comes from sonner. `<Toaster>` is mounted in `__root`, and `showError(text)` and `showSuccess(text)` in `ui/toast.ts` call `toast.custom` with the shared `ui/Toast`, whose `variant` sets the icon and the role: `error` is an alert with the danger icon, `success` a status with the check. They are plain functions so a hook's `onError` or `onSuccess` can call them. `test/setup.ts` calls `toast.dismiss()` after each test, because sonner keeps its toasts in module state outside the rendered tree and one test's toast would show up in the next.
- Loading: a part that reads data renders `data == null ? <SkeletonOf>…</SkeletonOf> : …`. `ui/SkeletonOf` wraps the real part filled with example data, kept per topic in `features/<topic>/*-examples.ts`, so the skeleton takes the part's own size. Skeletons are coarse: wrap a whole card (the featured session, each card of a folding section, each poll card, each list row, the slide, the header's name and avatar), never the inside of one. A card that joins several queries waits for all of them: `HomeFeaturedSession` shows the featured card as one skeleton until its active polls and, with featured questions on, its questions arrive. `.skeleton` paints the wrapped card as one soft grey block in the theme's colours and hides everything inside it, text, buttons and icons included. It adds the `.skeleton` class, `inert` and `aria-hidden`. It adds `aria-hidden` as well as `inert` because Testing Library ignores `inert`, and a screen reader must not read the example data.
- The login check does not block the page. `useMe` is built on `useApiQuery`, and components do the redirects: `_app` renders `<Navigate to="/setup">` for an incomplete profile, and the query client sends the user to the login on an access error.
- A query throws to the error boundary only when it has no data and the error is not an access error (`throwOnError` in `api/create-query-client.ts`); a failed refetch keeps the data already on screen. The router's `defaultErrorComponent` is `ui/ErrorScreen`, whose "Volver al inicio" calls `queryClient.resetQueries` on the queries in error before navigating home. Resetting React Query's error boundary is not enough: the reset lasts only until the first query mounts, so a page reached through a redirect, such as the teacher's `/admin` after `/`, mounts its query still in error and throws again.
- A query that only one role may run waits for the role with `enabled`. The API answers the other role with a 403, `NotStudent` or `NotTeacher`, which is not an access error. When the screen has no data yet, `throwOnError` sends that 403 to the error screen. On `/`, the student's sessions pass `enabled: me.data?.role === "student"`, so they wait for `me`, and the page draws the student's skeleton meanwhile. The featured card's polls and questions start once the sessions arrive, because `HomeFeaturedSession` mounts only then.
- `ui/Button` is the only text button, with variants `main`, `pill`, `pill-dark`, `pill-danger` and `pill-ghost` (a pill with no border or background, for the text actions that used to be underlined links; it takes the colour of the text around it, with a tint of that colour on hover, so it stays legible on the light cards in dark mode), and a `pending` prop with an optional `pendingLabel`. A pending button is disabled, shows a spinner and keeps its full colour. `Button` renders only a `<button>`. A link styled as a button is `ui/ButtonLink`, with the same variants and `to`/`params` typed per route as in the router's `Link`. `ButtonLink` renders the router's `Link`, so it navigates inside the app. Icon buttons (`icon-button`) stay outside both.
- The upload dialog and the material list check an HTML marked as slides with the same `useSlidesCheck` (`features/materials/`), and show its state with `SlidesCheckNotice`. The hook loads the HTML in a hidden `SlidesFrame` that the caller renders from `frame`. It shows the result no earlier than one second after `start`, so a fast check does not show and hide its notice at once. The list passes `okFor: 10_000`, so its ok notice goes away after 10 s; the dialog passes no `okFor`, so its ok notice has no time limit.
- `useClassroom` handles live classroom updates. Each WebSocket notice invalidates the keys of its topic, and data always comes through the hooks.
- Confirmations and overlays use the shared pieces in `ui/`. `ConfirmAction` holds the dialog's state (closed, asking, confirming, failed), takes a `renderTrigger`, an `onConfirm` and an `errorText`, and wraps `ConfirmDialog`. The dialog closes when `onConfirm` resolves and stays open with `errorText` when `onConfirm` rejects. `ConfirmDialog` takes `pending`, `pendingLabel` and `error`; while pending, Cancelar is disabled and neither Escape nor a click outside closes it. `Backdrop` draws the background of a sheet, an alert or the projected view, and closes on a click outside its content and on Escape.
- Escape closes only the topmost open backdrop. `useCloseOnEscape` keeps one shared stack of closers and one `keydown` listener; with one listener per backdrop, Escape would also close the sheet under a confirmation. The browser runs microtasks between listeners, so by the time the sheet's listener runs, the confirmation is gone and the sheet is on top.
- Folders follow the topic, not the file kind: `features/<topic>/` holds a topic's components and hooks together. Browser state helpers go in `helpers/` (`helpers/local-ui/`), shared UI in `ui/`.
- A component whose parts nobody else uses becomes a module, following the global wiki entry `react/component-modules`: a folder named after the component, with an `index.ts` that exports only that component, and one file per part beside it (`features/polls/PollResults/`). Code outside the folder imports from its `index.ts` only, never a part's file. The lint rule `kurasu-boundaries/module-entry` rejects an import that reaches into a folder holding an `index.ts`.
- Each file holds one component or hook, and uses named exports.
- Styles use Tailwind 4; the prototypes' colours and dark mode live in the theme.
- Repeated styles are classes in `@layer components` of `styles.css` (`main-button`, `pill-button`, `input-field`, `paper`, …). A class name must not match a utility Tailwind generates from a theme colour: a `.text-field` class got the `text-field` utility generated from `--color-field` as well, which painted the input's text white on a white field. The input class is `.input-field`.
- The UI is in Spanish; code is in English.

## Sources

- `.scratch/aula-virtual/program-design/kurasu.md`, branches 7 and 8, and its section "Implementación · diferencias con el diseño".
- `app/apps/web/src/api/api-error.ts`, `useApiQuery.ts`, `useApiMutation.ts`, `optimistic-patch.ts`, `create-query-client.ts`, `app/apps/web/src/ui/ConfirmAction.tsx`, `ConfirmDialog.tsx`, `Button.tsx`, `ButtonLink.tsx`, `SkeletonOf.tsx`, `ErrorScreen.tsx`, `Toast.tsx`, `toast.ts`, `Backdrop.tsx`, `useCloseOnEscape.ts`, `Field.tsx`, `FieldError.tsx`, `app/apps/web/src/helpers/useEmailForm.ts`, `app/apps/web/src/router.tsx`, `routes/_app.tsx`, `app/apps/web/src/styles.css`, `app/apps/web/test/setup.ts`, `app/apps/web/src/features/polls/useVote.ts`, `app/apps/web/src/features/materials/useSlidesCheck.ts`, `SlidesCheckNotice.tsx`, `app/apps/web/src/routes/_app/index.tsx`.
- `.scratch/email-valido/program-design/kurasu.md`, branches 3 and 4.
- `.scratch/ajustes-visuales/program-design/web.md`.
- `.scratch/aula-virtual/tasks.md`, T19, T21, T23 and T26; `.scratch/aula-virtual/reports/validate/index.html`, F1.

# Agentic review · kurasu (`app/`) · slides de a una y skeleton único

Changeset: working tree sin commitear sobre `feat/session-4-deck` (`e0f75d2`), `git diff HEAD`.

## Round 1

11 revisores (reuse, simplification, efficiency, altitude; conventions: wiki architecture, web, fence, react/component-modules, tanstack-query/operation-hooks, naming/booleans, app/AGENTS.md + estilo del usuario). 17 hallazgos.

### Fixes

- `TeacherSlides.tsx`, reuse: `isSame` repetía `samePosition` de `@kurasu/slides/navigation`; se usa `samePosition`.
- `TeacherSlides.tsx`, altitude + app-agents + simplification: la cola de guardado (refs, `moving`, `save`, `navigate`) sale a `features/classroom/useSlideMoves.ts`, que devuelve `{ position, navigate }`; el reset de fin de guardado queda en un solo `finish`, y `.then(onSaved, finish)` separa la falla del pedido de lo que pasa después.
- `useMoveSlide.ts`, wiki-web + tanstack-operation-hooks + altitude: el hook vuelve a escribir la sesión guardada en el cache en su `onSuccess` (cancela antes un refetch en curso), y en la falla la invalida. La pantalla ya no toca `useQueryClient` ni `queryKeys`.
- `routes/_app/index.tsx`, altitude + simplification + app-agents: la carga de la card destacada sale a `features/sessions/HomeFeaturedSession.tsx`, que pide encuestas y preguntas con el id de la sesión (sin `?? ""` ni `?? []`) y elige skeleton o card. La ruta elige solo entre skeleton, vacío y card.
- `routes/_app/index.tsx`, naming-booleans: `student` pasa a `isStudent`.
- `.mahou/wiki/web.md`, wiki-web: la excepción de mover la slide a las acciones al instante, la card que junta varias queries y qué espera a `me` en `/`.

### Skips

- Simplification 3, sacar `options` y el `export` de `SlideMove` en `useMoveSlide`: el revisor lo ve sin uso. Se salta porque el wiki `tanstack-query/operation-hooks` pide que cada hook de operación acepte sus opciones tipadas, y es así en todos los hooks.
- Efficiency 1, la card espera al más lento de los pedidos: es el comportamiento pedido por el usuario.
- Efficiency 2, una falla de encuestas o preguntas deja el skeleton: no pasa, porque una query sin datos que falla va a la pantalla de error (`throwOnError` en `create-query-client.ts`); falso positivo.

### Checks

`pnpm run check` pasa; `vitest run` de home-questions, admin-classroom, loading, home y vote-card: 79 tests pasan.
